subject: Solarflare capacity propensity check & temporary GPU hold request
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Solarflare capacity propensity check - late-stage

Team —

Solarflare (eng + procurement looped internally) is in the last mile for a Dedicated capacity contract. They asked for guidance on whether we can guarantee a steady block for their initial ramp: ~8x A100-equivalent GPUs sustained for 6 months, with an optional burst window.

Quick asks:
- Can infra confirm current available spare A100-equivalent capacity in us-west and us-east for Apr–Sep 2029?
- Can we place a temporary soft hold (non-billable) for up to 60 days while procurement finishes? If so, what is the hold policy (time, deposit, release conditions)?
- Any recommended fallback sizing/quantized model variants to present as lower-cost options?

I attached the draft mutual action plan from the AE to this thread. Need a concise capacity recommendation I can share with the customer by EOD.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber | Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0119
Redwood Inference

Attachment: mutual_action_plan_Solarflare.docx (draft)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Mar 2029 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Solarflare capacity propensity check - late-stage

Jonas —

Short answer: yes, we have headroom but with caveats. I pulled a snapshot of fleet utilization and warm spare capacity (attached). Highlights:

- Us-west (primary): ~10 A100-equivalent GPUs currently idle across two racks (node tags: usw-rack12-{n4,n5}), plus capacity that can be reclaimed from flexible pools if we accept 2–4 hour prewarm.
- Us-east (secondary): ~6 A100-equivalent GPUs idle but higher baseline utilization during business hours.
- Suggested soft hold: allocate 12 A100-equivalent units as a soft block (8 requested + 4 buffer) split across regions for redundancy (8 in us-west, 4 in us-east). Hold window: up to 60 days.

Operational notes / conditions:
- Soft holds are non-billable but require a written commitment to move to reserved capacity (or pay a one-time deposit) if the hold exceeds 45 days without a binding PO.
- We can pre-provision optimized quantized variants (8-bit) for ~25–35% cost savings; performance delta depends on model family. Recommend we map Solarflare's target model to the q4_0 quantization path as a lower-cost fallback.
- If they need guaranteed sub-50ms P95 latency at scale, that will require a dedicated pool with prewarmed GPUs and a service-level add-on.

I've attached capacity_snapshot_20290319.csv with node-level IDs and an initial bleed schedule. If you want, we can lock nodes under a conditional hold and mark them with deal tag SF-2029-1784.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin | Head of Compute Supply, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachment: capacity_snapshot_20290319.csv

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 19 Mar 2029 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Solarflare capacity propensity check - late-stage

Thanks Marcus — that aligns with what I expected. A few commercial points to call out before I loop the customer in:

- Solarflare's procurement timeline: target PO by 2029-04-15; they asked for hold through EOM Apr if possible.
- We should offer two hold tiers:
  1) Soft-hold (free) for 30 days with automatic release unless a PO is received.
  2) Conditional soft-hold (60 days) with a 20% refundable deposit or a written intent to purchase.

Jonas, when you share this with Emma/procurement, please present the fallback quantized plan and the deposit option. Also confirm whether the hold will block autoscaling for other customers (we should avoid hard-blocking; keep it as a tagged conditional-block).

I'll draft a short MAP (attached) and an outline for commercial terms.

—Laura

Hi Jonas and Laura —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Solarflare is comfortable with the 60-day conditional soft-hold provided we get:

- A written statement of the hold terms (time window, deposit amount, node reservation semantics).
- A one-page cost delta comparing full A100s vs the quantized fallback for our expected workload.
- A MAP that lays out milestones and the expected PO date (we'll try to hit 2029-04-12).

Can you also confirm whether a signed mutual action plan is sufficient to trigger the conditional hold, or if a financial deposit is strictly required for 60 days? Procurement asked for clarity before we commit.

Best,
Emma Park
VP Product, Solarflare AI
emma@solarflare.ai

Date: Wed, 20 Mar 2029 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Solarflare capacity propensity check - late-stage

Emma —

Appreciate the clarity. Per internal ops (Marcus) and commercial (Laura), Redwood can place a conditional soft-hold for up to 60 days under two options:

Option A (preferred): 60-day conditional hold triggered by a signed Mutual Action Plan + 20% refundable deposit. Deposit protects capacity reclamation cost and prewarming ops.
Option B: 30-day free soft-hold triggered by signed MAP only (no deposit).

I'll attach the one-page cost delta and the MAP for you to sign. If you sign MAP and submit deposit within 5 business days, we will tag the nodes as SF-2029-1784 and mark them as a conditional block. Nodes will remain available for hot-standby but will not be reallocated without a 48-hour notice.

Next steps:
- I uploaded the MAP here: https://www.docusign.com/solarflare/SF-1784/hold-request
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DF-1784 (I'll update with the hold milestone)
- Internal ops runbook for holds: internal://runbooks/gpu-hold-playbook-v2

Tell me which option Solarflare prefers and I will route the DocuSign.

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Emma Park <emma@solarflare.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2029 15:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Solarflare capacity propensity check - late-stage

Looping in a couple of technical constraints so we have alignment before the hold is confirmed:

- Autoscale behavior: the conditional block will be a tagged reservation; autoscale is not hard-disabled. If other customers spike, prewarmed nodes may be reclaimed with 48-hour notice as Jonas noted. For strict QoS we need a reserved pool (adds cost).
- Prewarming: we will provision an image and pre-cache weights on the reserved nodes. That adds ~2–6 hours lead time per node for initial warm-up.
- Quantization path: recommend q4_0 for the fallback; engineering validated latency/throughput tradeoffs for Solarflare's target model family in the internal eval last quarter.

I'll update the runbook entry for SF-2029-1784 and tag the candidate nodes. If Solarflare signs the MAP today we can mark the soft-block and start prewarming tomorrow morning.

—Karthik
